title: Framing the Constitution: The Beginning of a New Era

topics.title: A Tumultuous Time and the Making of the Constituent Assembly

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the political situation of 1945-47, including popular upsurges, Partition violence and the problem of the princely states, in which the Constituent Assembly met.
Explain how the members of the Constituent Assembly were chosen and why the Congress dominated it.
Identify the roles played by Nehru, Patel, Rajendra Prasad and Ambedkar in the Constituent Assembly.
Recognise the members of the Drafting Committee and the civil servants who assisted the framing of the Constitution.

topics.title: The Vision of the Constitution: The Objectives Resolution

concepts.learning_objective: State the ideals proclaimed in the Objectives Resolution moved by Nehru on 13 December 1946.
Interpret Nehru's argument that India would learn from other revolutions and democracies without merely copying them.
Explain Somnath Lahiri's criticism that the Constituent Assembly worked under the shadow of British power.
Explain Nehru's claim that the Assembly drew its strength from the will of the people and the social struggles behind it.
Distinguish the colonial Acts of 1909, 1919 and 1935 from the constitution-making of 1946-49.

topics.title: Defining Rights: The Problem with Separate Electorates

concepts.learning_objective: Describe B. Pocker Bahadur's case for continuing separate electorates for Muslims.
Analyse the arguments of Patel, Pant and others against separate electorates and their concern for a unified nation.

topics.title: Protection for the Poor, Tribals and Depressed Castes

concepts.learning_objective: Explain N.G. Ranga's view that the real minorities were the poor and downtrodden masses.
Describe Jaipal Singh's arguments for protecting tribals through reservation of seats.
Explain the demands of Depressed Caste members and the measures finally recommended by the Assembly.
Describe the three lists of subjects, Article 356 and the fiscal provisions of the Constitution.
Explain K. Santhanam's arguments for giving greater powers to the provinces.
Analyse why most members, especially after Partition, argued for a strong Centre.

topics.title: The Language of the Nation, Universal Franchise and Secularism

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why Mahatma Gandhi wanted Hindustani, a composite language, to be the national language.
Describe the Hindi debate, the fears of non-Hindi speakers and the Language Committee's compromise formula.
Evaluate universal adult franchise and the Indian idea of secularism as features of the Constitution.
